blocks.label: text
blocks.text: also described the life history of Pholoe anoculata from North Carolina. Brood care within the elytra is known in Laubierpholoe (Figs. 7.3d, e) (Laubier, 1975; Pettibone, 1992; Westheide, 2001) and in brood sacs under the elytra in Taylorpholoe (Pettibone, 1992; Wolf, 1986b).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Natural history of Sigalionidae is poorly studied. They are found worldwide and occur from the intertidal to depths of several thousand metres. Pisioninae are mostly found in shallow waters, with Pisione longipalpa described from >900m (Uschakov, 1956) being the only exception. All Pisioninae and some Pholoinae (Metaxypsamma, Laubierpholoe, Imajimapholoe, Taylorpholoe) are interstitial. Pisione garciavaldecasasi is the only known freshwater species and was described from rivers in Panama (San Martin et al., 1998).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In general, Sigalionidae, considering their jaw morphology, are expected to be carnivorous. However, feeding habits of Sigalionidae are largely unknown. Most Sigalioninae burrow in soft sediments and Sthenelanella inhabits self-constructed tubes. This indicates that they are likely to be sit-and-wait predators (Jumars et al., 2015). In fact, Pernet (2000) described such behaviour for Sthenelais berkeleyi, where the animals burrow into the sediment and use antero-dorsally oriented chaetae to form a 'chaetal snorkel' to maintain respiration. Pholoinae are most probably more active hunter predators. Pleijel (1983), in the only study on the feeding biology of Pholoinae, described Pholoe baltica (as Pholoe minuta) as an active predator on Spionidae, small crustaceans, and forams. If active predation also occurs in other Sigalionidae, this remains to be shown. Heffernan et al. (1983) reported mean densities of about 100 per 0.1 m² of Pholoe baltica (as Pholoe minuta) from Ireland. Gonzalez et al. (2017a) discuss the biogeographical distribution patterns of Pisione.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Sigalionidae have a convoluted taxonomic history. Historically, the group included scale-worms bearing compound neurochaetae, corresponding largely to today's Sigalioninae. Rouse and Fauchald's (1997) cladistic analyses recovered Sigalionidae as the sister group to other Aphroditiformia that lacked compound neurochaetae. However, subsequent analyses based on both morphology (Pleijel and Dahlgren, 1998; Rouse and Pleijel, 2001) and also sequence data (Gonzalez et al., 2018a; Norlinder et al., 2012; Struck et al., 2005b; Wiklund et al., 2005; Zhang, Y. et al., 2018a) repeatedly revealed the paraphyly of Sigalionidae, both with regard to Pholoinae and Pisioninae.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the most recent phylogenetic studies of Aphroditiformia by Zhang et al., (2018a) and Gonzalez et al. (2018a), Sigalionidae was recovered as the sister group to a clade comprising Polynoidae + (Iphionidae + Acoetidae). Gonzalez et al. (2018a) also revised the classification of Aphroditiformia and there Sigalionidae was subdivided into Pelogeniinae, Pisioninae, Pholoinae, Sigalioninae, and Sthenelanellinae. We here follow their delineation of the group, though not all the names. This makes the first described Sigalionidae to be Pholoe longa (Müller, 1776) (as Aphrodita longa). The phylogenetic relationships within Sigalionidae remain problematic and warrant further study (Gonzalez et al., 2018a).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Sthenelanellinae is monotypic for Sthenelanella, making one of the names currently superfluous and we therefore use the latter only. The type species Sthenelanella uniformis was first named by Moore (1910) and later the genus was revised by Pettibone (1969b). Currently, there are only six recognized species of Sthenelanella (Read and Fauchald, 2021). Pettibone (1997) erected Pelogeniinae for Pelogenia, Psammolyce, Neopsammolyce, Hartmanipsammolyce, Dayipsammolyce, Claparedepelogenia, Pottsipelogenia, and Heteropelogenia, and these are the genera considered valid today (Gonzalez et al., 2018a). Pisioninae include the taxa Anoplopisione, Pisione, Pisionella, and Pisionidens (Gonzalez et al., 2017b). The most species-rich group within Pisioninae is Pisione with 46 species out of a total of 54 (Read and Fauchald, 2021). Generic diagnoses for all Sigalionidae (excl. Pisioninae) are provided in Eibye-Jacobsen et al. (2018) and separately for Pisioninae in Gonzalez et al. (2017b).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Both Pholoinae and Sigalioninae also have complicated taxonomic histories. The former taxon currently includes Ima-jimapholoë, Laubierpholoë, Metaxypsamma, Pholoë, and Taylorpholoë. Pholoinae were in earlier literature either treated as a subgroup within Sigalionidae (e.g. Chamberlin, 1919; Levinsen, 1883), or as a separate group (see review in Pettibone, 1992). The family names Pholoididae and Peisidicidae were introduced by Fauchald (1977) and Darboux (1900), respectively, but synonymized with Pholoidae by Pettibone (1992). Sigalioninae correspond largely to what was referred to as Sigalionidae in earlier literature. Sigalioninae encompasses 14 genera, and now also include Pholoides (Gonzalez et al., 2018a). Read and Fauchald (2021) accept 249 species in Sigalionidae sensu Gonzalez et al. (2018a).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Important early studies include Ehlers (1864) and Darboux (1899). Major taxonomic studies include a series of revisions by Pettibone (1969b; Pettibone 1970a; b; c; Pettibone 1971a; b), and Mackie and Chambers (1990). Regional studies on Sigalionidae are provided by Lana (1991b) for Brazil, Blake (1995b) for California, Wehe (2007) from around the Arabian Peninsula, and Chambers (1985), Hartmann-Schröder (1996), Chambers and Muir (1997) for northern Europe. Sigalion recorded from northern Europe were reviewed by Muir (1989). An annotated checklist of Sigalionidae and Pholoidae was published by Aungtonya and Eibye-Jacobsen (2014). Most recent taxonomic additions to the group include Martinez et al., (2008) and Petersen et al., (2016) for Pisioninae, Aungtonya (2007), Padovanni and Amaral (2014), Alalykina (2018), and Aungtonya and Eibye-Jacobsen (2018) for Sigalioninae. Barnich and Van Haaren (2021) have published a detailed revision of Northeast Atlantic and Mediterranean Sigalioninae and provide an updated identification key. Meissner et al., (2017) used an integrative taxonomic approach to address the diversity of Arctic Pholoepp, including redescriptions of Pholoe longa and Pholo minuta. Dryptoscolex matthiesae is a Carboniferous-aged fossil described by Thompson (1979). Fitzhugh et al. (1997) considered it as part of Sigalionidae owing to Thompson's (1979) suggestion that compound chaetae were present.
